title: 420. Britain in 1974: Thatcher Enters the Ring (Part 4)

sentences.en: Saturday, the 5th of October, 1974, was a big night for Paul Cray and Carol Burns.
sentences.zh: 1974年10月5日星期六，对保罗·克雷和卡罗尔·伯恩斯来说是一个重要的夜晚。

sentences.en: By coincidence, their birthdays fell on the same day.
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，他们的生日在同一天。

sentences.en: And Paul, who was due to turn 22, thought it would be nice to have a little party.
sentences.zh: 保罗即将满22岁，他觉得办个小派对会很不错。

sentences.en: Only a few weeks earlier, Carol, three years his junior, had been accepted into the Women's Royal Army Corps.
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，比他小三岁的卡罗尔刚被英国皇家女子陆军部队录取。

sentences.en: So they had something special to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有一些特别的事情要庆祝。

sentences.en: She chose the venue, a pub not far from her barracks, recommended by some of her new friends who used to meet their boyfriends there on Saturday nights.
sentences.zh: 她选了地点，那是离她军营不远的一家酒吧，是她的一些新朋友推荐的，她们过去常在周六晚上在那里见男朋友。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Paul had a surprise up his sleeve.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，保罗还准备了一个惊喜。

sentences.en: Unbeknown to Carol, he had invited her parents down from Boreham Wood for the evening, and when she left headquarters, all three of them were waiting outside to greet her.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔不知道，他邀请了她的父母从博勒姆伍德赶来参加晚会，当她离开总部时，他们三个人都在外面等着迎接她。

sentences.en: They walked onto the pub, the horse and groom in Guildford, which was already filling up.
sentences.zh: 他们走进那家酒吧，位于吉尔福德的“马与新郎”，里面已经快坐满了。

sentences.en: The atmosphere was noisy, happy.
sentences.zh: 气氛嘈杂而欢乐。

sentences.en: Many of the drinkers were soldiers and their girlfriends, enjoying a night out.
sentences.zh: 许多酒客都是士兵和他们的女朋友，正在享受夜晚的时光。

sentences.en: The Burns family found a table in an alcove by the jukebox.
sentences.zh: 伯恩斯一家在点唱机旁的一个凹室里找到了座位。

sentences.en: Carol disappeared to the toilet for a minute or two.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔消失了一两分钟去上厕所。

sentences.en: When she came back, Paul had moved up and taken her seat, so she slipped in beside him.
sentences.zh: 当她回来时，保罗已经挪动位置坐到了她的位子上，所以她滑到他身边坐下。

sentences.en: It was almost nine o'clock.
sentences.zh: 当时快九点了。

sentences.en: Then, quite suddenly, there was a gigantic bang, and everything went black.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，一声巨响，一切都陷入了黑暗。

sentences.en: The next thing Carol knew, she was lying on the ground, her ears full of buzzing, her mouth full of smoke and duSt.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔醒来时，发现自己躺在地上，耳朵里嗡嗡作响，嘴里满是烟尘。

sentences.en: Someone was lying on the floor beside me, she said later.
sentences.zh: 她后来回忆说，有人躺在我身边的地板上。

sentences.en: It was Paul.
sentences.zh: 那是保罗。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, that is from your history of Britain in 1974 to 1979, Seasons in the Sun.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，这段内容出自你关于1974年至1979年英国历史的著作《阳光下的季节》。

sentences.en: And it describes what has been commemorated as the Guildford pub bombing.
sentences.zh: 它描述了后来被称为“吉尔福德酒吧爆炸案”的事件。

sentences.en: So, Paul is dead?
sentences.zh: 所以，保罗死了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Paul was killed trace away.
sentences.zh: 保罗当场死亡。

sentences.en: He's one of five people killed that evening.
sentences.zh: 他是那天晚上遇难的五个人之一。

sentences.en: 5th of October 1974, there was a bomb in the alcove that you mentioned by the jukebox that had been planted by the provisional IRA.
sentences.zh: 1974年10月5日，你提到的点唱机旁的凹室里有一枚炸弹，是临时派别爱尔兰共和军放置的。

sentences.en: It's a reminder of how chance matters in history, because when Carol went to the toilet, they moved places.
sentences.zh: 这提醒了我们偶然性在历史中有多重要，因为当卡罗尔去上厕所时，他们换了位置。

sentences.en: If she was still sitting where she had been, she would have been killed, not Paul.
sentences.zh: 如果她还坐在原来的位置，死的就是她，而不是保罗。

sentences.en: Her parents were very badly injured.
sentences.zh: 她的父母受了重伤。

sentences.en: Her father, I think, was in a coma for five weeks.
sentences.zh: 我想她的父亲昏迷了五周。

sentences.en: Four other people were killed.
sentences.zh: 另有四人死亡。

sentences.en: 68 people injured.
sentences.zh: 68人受伤。

sentences.en: Two of the people who died were teenagers, teenage girls who'd also joined the Women's Royal Army Corps, and two teenage boys, Scots Guards, Sir William Forsyth and James Hunter,
sentences.zh: 死者中有两名十几岁的少女，她们也加入了英国皇家女子陆军部队，还有两名十几岁的苏格兰卫队士兵，威廉·福赛斯爵士和詹姆斯·亨特，

sentences.en: who were friends from the same street in Renfrewshire, who had only joined up a month beforehand.
sentences.zh: 他们是来自伦弗鲁郡同一条街的朋友，才入伍一个月。

sentences.en: And the Guildford pub bombing sent an absolute shockwave through Britain.
sentences.zh: 吉尔福德酒吧爆炸案在英国引起了巨大的震动。

sentences.en: There have been many bombings, of course, in Northern Ireland in the last couple of years, but this was seen as something, a bomb in a pub in Britain, in the home counties,
sentences.zh: 当然，过去几年北爱尔兰发生过许多爆炸案，但这被视为一件大事，在英国本土、在内陆郡的酒吧里发生爆炸，

sentences.en: was seen as unbelievably shocking.
sentences.zh: 被认为令人难以置信地震惊。

sentences.en: And of course, what made it more shocking, Tom, was that afterwards, the police charged four innocent people who went to prison for 15 years.
sentences.zh: 当然，汤姆，更令人震惊的是，事后警方指控了四名无辜者，他们入狱了15年。

sentences.en: Yeah, because that's what it's chiefly remembered for now, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，因为这正是它现在最被人记住的原因，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And almost certainly the culprits were a group called the Balcom Street Gang, who were a provisional IRA unit who were kind of on the loose in England in 1974 and 1975,
sentences.zh: 而且几乎可以肯定，罪魁祸首是一个叫“巴尔科姆街帮”的组织，他们是临时派爱尔兰共和军的一个小组，1974年和1975年在英国流窜，

sentences.en: and who actually said at their trial in 1977, there were innocent people in prison for the Guildford pub bombing, but the police and so on didn't listen.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上在1977年的审判中说，有无辜的人因为吉尔福德酒吧爆炸案而入狱，但警方并没有听取。

sentences.en: So yeah, it's a pretty shocking story.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，这是一个相当令人震惊的故事。

sentences.en: We're at the final episode of this 1974 marathon, and this is five days before the general election campaign, the second general election in 1974, which is where we ended,
sentences.zh: 我们正处于这次1974年马拉松节目的最后一集，距离大选竞选还有五天，这是1974年的第二次大选，也就是我们上次结束的地方，

sentences.en: didn't we, last time?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Harold Wilson has decided on the showdown with Ted Heath to try and give himself the mandate, because he's been leading a minority government,
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·威尔逊决定与泰德·希思进行摊牌，试图给自己争取授权，因为他一直领导着一个少数派政府，

sentences.en: and this sort of darkness overshadows the election.
sentences.zh: 而这种黑暗笼罩着选举。

sentences.en: And you described in the previous episode how Wilson is seen by many people on the right as so illegitimate as actually to be potentially a Soviet mole.
sentences.zh: 你在上一集中描述了威尔逊是如何被右翼的许多人视为如此非法，以至于实际上可能是苏联的间谍。

sentences.en: People on the left are talking with some justification of the possibility of a right-wing coup.
sentences.zh: 左翼人士则有理有据地谈论着右翼政变的可能性。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there is a sense of extreme polarisation in the country, and then to have this act of brutal violence, as you say, in the home counties in Surrey,
sentences.zh: 所以这个国家有一种极端的两极分化感，然后又发生了这种残酷的暴力行为，正如你所说，在萨里郡的内陆地区，

sentences.en: one of the richest and most prosperous areas in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这是英国最富裕、最繁荣的地区之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I assume then that it must have radically enhanced the sense that many people have, that this is a state of crisis like none that Britain has faced since the war.
sentences.zh: 我假设这一定从根本上加强了许多人的感觉，即这是一种战后英国从未面临过的危机状态。

sentences.en: I think what it doesn't do is to create a sort of, what you might call a histrionic or extreme reaction.
sentences.zh: 我认为它没有造成所谓的歇斯底里或极端的反应。

sentences.en: Actually, what it adds to is a sense, I think, of weariness, of depression.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为它增加了一种疲惫和压抑的感觉。

sentences.en: Because don't forget, the conflict in Northern Ireland has been going on since the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 因为别忘了，北爱尔兰的冲突从20世纪60年代末就开始了。

sentences.en: So we're into kind of year five a bit now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在已经进入了第五个年头。

sentences.en: And most people don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 大多数人并不理解它。

sentences.en: Most people in Great Britain don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 英国的大多数人并不理解它。

sentences.en: They don't really care, to be brutally honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他们并不真正关心。

sentences.en: But they are horrified by it, and by the fact that it is, as they see it, seeping into the life of...
sentences.zh: 但他们对此感到恐惧，而且因为正如他们所见，它正在渗透到……的生活中。

sentences.en: So the Times actually says that, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以《泰晤士报》实际上是这么说的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It says that no election since the war had been held in such a mood of public uncertainty and depression.
sentences.zh: 它说战后没有任何一次选举是在如此公众不确定和压抑的情绪下举行的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So depression rather than anger.
sentences.zh: 所以是压抑而不是愤怒。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, there is anger, as we will see later on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有愤怒，正如我们稍后会看到的。

sentences.en: There are people who are calling for the death penalty for terrorists, because the death penalty had been done away with just a few years earlier.
sentences.zh: 有人呼吁对恐怖分子判处死刑，因为死刑在几年前才被废除。

sentences.en: But I think it adds to a sense of kind of world weariness, of shabbiness, of ineffectual government, and a sense of helplessness, actually, I guess is the word, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这增加了一种世界性的疲惫感、破败感、政府的无能，以及一种无助感，我想这才是那个词，汤姆。

sentences.en: That Britain is now, having been for so long, the great actor on the world stage, that for the first time, I think, in the mid-1970s,
sentences.zh: 英国长期以来一直是世界舞台上的伟大主角，而在20世纪70年代中期，我认为这是第一次，

sentences.en: people realized that Britain is actually on the receiving end of change and of major geopolitical developments.
sentences.zh: 人们意识到英国实际上正处于变革和重大地缘政治发展的承受端。

sentences.en: And there's a sense of impotence, I think, impotence of the government to do anything about Northern Ireland,
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种无力感，政府对北爱尔兰问题无能为力，

sentences.en: but impotence to do with inflation or the pace of globalization and de-industrialization and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 对通货膨胀、全球化步伐、去工业化以及所有这些事情也无能为力。

sentences.en: And is there a sense also of, I might almost say boredom, tedium, a sense that this is just an endless cycle of two rather shop-soiled leaders in the form of Wilson and Heath?
sentences.zh: 是否还有一种感觉，我甚至可以说是一种无聊、乏味，感觉这只是威尔逊和希思这两个相当陈旧的领导人之间无休止的循环？

sentences.en: Neither of them are inspirational.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都无法鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: Neither of them really seem to promise a kind of radical change.
sentences.zh: 他们两人似乎都没有真正承诺某种激进的变革。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: So Wilson, who we talked about a lot last time, the sort of chaotics, I mean, some people might think we were being a bit harsh on Wilson,
sentences.zh: 所以威尔逊，我们上次谈了很多关于他的混乱，我的意思是，有些人可能认为我们对威尔逊有点苛刻，

sentences.en: that sort of chaotic six-month period after he became prime minister.
sentences.zh: 他在成为首相后那混乱的六个月。

sentences.en: But actually, the chaos really continues into the election campaign.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这种混乱确实延续到了竞选活动中。

sentences.en: So the very first meeting of his election team, Tom, has to be moved from room to room because Marcia Williams, who played such a leading role in the last episode,
sentences.zh: 所以他的竞选团队的第一次会议，汤姆，不得不从一个房间搬到另一个房间，因为玛莎·威廉姆斯，她在上一集中扮演了如此重要的角色，

sentences.en: she's very keen that her nemeses, I mean, his high command to her, Joe Haynes, his press secretary, and Bernard Donahue, his policy chief.
sentences.zh: 她非常热衷于对付她的宿敌，我的意思是，他的高级指挥部，乔·海恩斯，他的新闻秘书，以及伯纳德·多纳休，他的政策主管。

sentences.en: I mean, to be fair, they have been plotting to murder her.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，他们一直在密谋杀害她。

sentences.en: They have, right.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是，对吧。

sentences.en: But they've been discussing plotting to murder her.
sentences.zh: 但他们一直在讨论密谋杀害她。

sentences.en: They haven't actually been plotting.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有真正实施密谋。

sentences.en: I think that's semantic.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是语义问题。

sentences.en: She doesn't want them to come to the meetings, so she keeps changing the room behind their back.
sentences.zh: 她不想让他们参加会议，所以她一直在背着他们更换房间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that sort of behavior.
sentences.zh: 就是那种行为。

sentences.en: Also, Wilson gets tanked up on brandy before his first TV broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 此外，威尔逊在第一次电视广播前喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: So there's that sort of sense of general seediness and shabbiness and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种普遍的肮脏、破败等等的感觉。

sentences.en: So Wilson's having all kinds of trouble with Marcia.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔逊在玛莎身上遇到了各种麻烦。

sentences.en: What about, so there's Tony Benn, who's been picking up all kinds of, basically is foisting policies on Wilson that he doesn't really want.
sentences.zh: 那么托尼·本呢，他一直在收集各种东西，基本上是把威尔逊并不真正想要的政策强加给他。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Wilson doesn't really want to go into that election with any policies at all, right, Tom?
sentences.zh: 威尔逊并不真的想带着任何政策参加那次选举，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Because Wilson's great thing you said about people being bored.
sentences.zh: 因为你说的关于人们感到无聊，那是威尔逊的伟大之处。

sentences.en: Wilson wants people to be bored.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊希望人们感到无聊。

sentences.en: Because his promise is, I will give you a quiet life.
sentences.zh: 因为他的承诺是，我会给你们平静的生活。

sentences.en: No more conflict with the unions.
sentences.zh: 不再与工会发生冲突。

sentences.en: We've got our lovely social contract, which fans of Russo will remember from the last episode, where we will basically give the unions the pay deals they want.
sentences.zh: 我们有可爱的社会契约，鲁索的粉丝会记得上一集提到的，我们基本上会给工会他们想要的工资协议。

sentences.en: And we will then give them lots of extra goodies, like health and safety stuff and all these things.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会给他们很多额外的好处，比如健康和安全方面的东西以及所有这些。

sentences.en: And in return, they will moderate their future pay demands.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，他们会缓和未来的加薪要求。

sentences.en: Tony Benn, on the other hand, is the great apostle of nationalization, of a national enterprise board, of state planning, and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，托尼·本是国有化、国家企业委员会、国家计划以及所有这些东西的伟大倡导者。

sentences.en: And he is the great bogeyman.
sentences.zh: 他是那个大魔头。

sentences.en: And Wilson basically tries to keep him in a box throughout the election campaign.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊基本上在整个竞选期间都试图把他关在盒子里。

sentences.en: And there are all these stories that keep coming into Labour High Command, that the newspapers are preparing these amazing revelations about Tony Benn, that he's a drug addict.
sentences.zh: 而且一直有各种故事传到工党高层，说报纸正在准备关于托尼·本的惊人揭露，说他是瘾君子。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, Tony Benn is the most abstemious of men, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，托尼·本是最节制的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 他是。

sentences.en: He's a teetotaler.
sentences.zh: 他滴酒不沾。

sentences.en: He loves his tea.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢喝茶。

sentences.en: He loves his tea, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢喝茶，汤姆。

sentences.en: But nothing more than that.
sentences.zh: 但仅此而已。

sentences.en: And he also, as we discovered when he appeared in The Rest is History's second historical Love Island, he very much loves his wife, Caroline.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我们在他出现在《历史的其余部分》的第二个历史版“恋爱岛”时所发现的那样，他非常爱他的妻子卡罗琳。

sentences.en: It's one of the great philosophical love stories.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的哲学爱情故事之一。

sentences.en: But the newspapers also had apparently prepared this story that he was taking part in orgies at a place called Bickenhall Mansions, which is in Marleybone,
sentences.zh: 但报纸显然也准备了一个故事，说他正在马里波恩的一个叫比肯霍尔公寓的地方参加狂欢派对，

sentences.en: an Edwardian mansion block.
sentences.zh: 那是一座爱德华时代的公寓大楼。

sentences.en: A Sunday Mirror editor passed this story to Harold Wilson, and Wilson called Ben in, and he said, sort of smoked his pipe at him, and said, Is it true?
sentences.zh: 《星期日镜报》的一位编辑把这个故事传给了哈罗德·威尔逊，威尔逊把本叫来，一边对他抽着烟斗，一边说，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Have you been taking part in orgies in these?
sentences.zh: 你一直在参加这些狂欢派对吗？

sentences.en: And Ben was very offended by this, because obviously he hadn't.
sentences.zh: 本对此感到非常冒犯，因为显然他没有。

sentences.en: Well, he would be, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他当然会这样。

sentences.en: And is this the point where the tabloids really start going after Tony Benn?
sentences.zh: 这是小报真正开始针对托尼·本的时候吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because from this point on, he will be the great hate object, won't he?
sentences.zh: 因为从这一点开始，他将成为那个伟大的仇恨对象，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's the standard bearer of what the tabloids call the loony left.
sentences.zh: 他是小报所说的“疯狂左派”的旗手。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they don't really coin the loony left phrase for another 10 years, but absolutely at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在大约10年后才创造出“疯狂左派”这个词，但绝对是在这一点上。

sentences.en: They're calling him a commissar, a Bolshevik, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们称他为政委、布尔什维克，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And actually, Wilson goes out of his way to sort of basically hide Ben under a massive blanket for the next few weeks during the election campaign.
sentences.zh: 实际上，威尔逊竭尽全力在接下来的几周竞选期间基本上把本藏在一张巨大的毯子下。

sentences.en: So that's all very, very inspiring.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都非常、非常鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, what about Edward Heath?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，爱德华·希思怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, so Ted Heath, fans of Ted Heath will have not enjoyed the previous episode because he was absent.
sentences.zh: 嗯，泰德·希思的粉丝们可能不会喜欢上一集，因为他缺席了。

sentences.en: He was off sulking.
sentences.zh: 他去生闷气了。

sentences.en: He's been defeated.
sentences.zh: 他被打败了。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say Ted Heath isn't the most busted of busted flushes going into the October 1974 campaign, because he never thought he was going to lose, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，泰德·希思在参加1974年10月的竞选时并不是最彻底的失败者，因为他从没想过自己会输，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That first election.
sentences.zh: 那第一次选举。

sentences.en: And now I know this is a sad moment for you because you're a man of Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道这对你来说是一个悲伤的时刻，因为你是索尔兹伯里人。

sentences.en: Ted Heath, of course, famously went to live in Salisbury, a great Wiltsherman.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思当然很有名地去索尔兹伯里居住，是一位伟大的威尔特郡人。

sentences.en: I don't know if you like yachting and piano playing and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否喜欢游艇和弹钢琴之类的东西。

sentences.en: I don't really like yachting, no.
sentences.zh: 我不怎么喜欢游艇，不。

sentences.en: But his yacht crashes, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但他的游艇撞毁了，不是吗？

sentences.en: A couple of months before the election.
sentences.zh: 在选举前几个月。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's unbelievably unlucky.
sentences.zh: 是的，他倒霉得难以置信。

sentences.en: He's got an undiagnosed thyroid complaint, Heath.
sentences.zh: 希思患有未确诊的甲状腺疾病。

sentences.en: His yacht, Morning Cloud, sank at the Isle of Wight and two people died on there, one of whom was his godson.
sentences.zh: 他的游艇“晨云号”在怀特岛沉没，船上有两人死亡，其中一人是他的教子。

sentences.en: So that's a very bad business.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一件非常糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is sad.
sentences.zh: 是的，那确实很悲伤。

sentences.en: And he has clung on to the Tory leadership like a limp at all through the summer.
sentences.zh: 整个夏天，他就像个软脚虾一样紧紧抓着保守党领袖的位置不放。

sentences.en: He does, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 确实是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: He goes to visit Chairman Mao, who gives him a couple of pandas.
sentences.zh: 他去拜访毛主席，毛主席送了他几只大熊猫。

sentences.en: Pandas, yeah.
sentences.zh: 大熊猫，没错。

sentences.en: Has that not boosted his profile?
sentences.zh: 这难道没有提升他的形象吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: One of his friends said Mao was the first person he'd seen in months who was actually pleased to see him,
sentences.zh: 他的一位朋友说，毛主席是他几个月来见到的第一个真正乐意见到他的人，

sentences.en: a harsh thing for one of your friends to say about you.
sentences.zh: 朋友这么评价你，还真是够刻薄的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is harsh.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实刻薄。

sentences.en: Now, the thing that Ted Heath and the Tories do in October 1974, Tom, which you will enjoy,
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，泰德·希思和保守党在1974年10月做的那件事，你会感兴趣的，

sentences.en: because you're very much a kind of, I mean, without being mean to you, you're a centrist dad, aren't you, ultimately?
sentences.zh: 因为你很大程度上属于那种——我不是要冒犯你——你本质上是个中间派老爸，对吧？

sentences.en: I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想是吧。

sentences.en: And Ted Heath runs the ultimate, the absolutely ultimate centrist dad, Rory Stewart, rest his politics campaign.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思推出了终极的、绝对的中间派老爸——罗里·斯图尔特，来开展他的政治竞选活动。

sentences.en: Well, I can't wait to see if it sweeps him to power.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我迫不及待想看看这是否能让他上台。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you can gauge from that how effective it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 你可以从这里看出这会有多大成效。

sentences.en: So what's the manifestation of this centrist dad manifesto?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个中间派老爸的宣言具体是什么呢？

sentences.en: First of all, his aides say to him, you were too abrasive in February 1974.
sentences.zh: 首先，他的助手对他说，你在1974年2月表现得太生硬了。

sentences.en: Take off your suit.
sentences.zh: 把你的西装脱掉。

sentences.en: Remember that Rory Stewart took off his tie.
sentences.zh: 记得罗里·斯图尔特脱掉了领带吗？

sentences.en: He did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他确实脱了，没错。

sentences.en: So the sartorial element is important here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的着装元素很重要。

sentences.en: Take off your suit and go around the country in your shirt sleeves, or indeed in a cuddly jumper.
sentences.zh: 脱掉西装，穿着衬衫袖子，或者干脆穿件舒适的毛衣在全国各地走动。

sentences.en: And being a vuncular, friendly, jovial fellow.
sentences.zh: 做一个和蔼可亲、友好、风趣的人。

sentences.en: Now, Ted Heath is not a jovial man, but also they say, listen, we're not going to win as just ourselves.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思本人并不是个风趣的人，但他们还说，听着，光靠我们自己是赢不了的。

sentences.en: We have to say that we stand for, and this is where your rest is politics comes in, a national unity coalition government, a sensible government.
sentences.zh: 我们必须表明我们的立场——这就是你那档“政治的本质”节目的用武之地了——我们要建立一个民族团结联合政府，一个理性的政府。

sentences.en: You know, let's get people together around the table.
sentences.zh: 你知道，让我们把大家聚到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Put aside the partisan bickering.
sentences.zh: 抛开党派纷争。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So he's got all his ministers.
sentences.zh: 所以他召集了他所有的部长。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Can I ask you about one particular minister and how-
sentences.zh: 我能问你关于其中一位部长以及她如何——

sentences.en: Who's it going to be?
sentences.zh: 会是谁呢？

sentences.en: How she-
sentences.zh: 她如何——

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了。

sentences.en: How she reacts to this.
sentences.zh: 她对这件事的反应。

sentences.en: And this is the education secretary, Mrs. Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 那就是教育大臣，撒切尔夫人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she had not been a great star of Heath's government, I wouldn't have said.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得她之前并不是希思政府里的明星人物。

sentences.en: They're quite similar, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们俩挺像的，不是吗？

sentences.en: So they're both from kind of petty bourgeois backgrounds, one might say.
sentences.zh: 他们都出身于小资产阶级背景，可以这么说。

sentences.en: Yeah, but slightly different.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但略有不同。

sentences.en: Hers is a little bit more respectable.
sentences.zh: 她的背景稍微体面一点。

sentences.en: Her father was an alderman and ran a shop.
sentences.zh: 她父亲是市议员，还经营着一家店。

sentences.en: Ted Heath's father was basically a builder.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思的父亲基本上是个建筑工人。

sentences.en: And I think as a result, she is much keener to trumpet her background than Ted Heath is.
sentences.zh: 我认为正因如此，她比泰德·希思更热衷于宣扬自己的出身。

sentences.en: So Ted Heath has been embarrassed about his background and rebrands himself as a patrician.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思对自己的出身感到尴尬，于是把自己重新包装成贵族派。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher is a sort of sharp, elbowed, aspirational, lower middle class warrior in a way that Heath isn't really.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人则是一个精明、好胜、有抱负的下中产阶级斗士，而希思并不完全是这样。

sentences.en: But at this point-
sentences.zh: 但在这一点上——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, is she enthusiastically supporting Heath's manifesto and election plan?
sentences.zh: 我是说，她是在热情地支持希思的宣言和竞选计划吗？

sentences.en: Is she piling in or is she off having nothing to do with it?
sentences.zh: 她是全力投入，还是置身事外？

sentences.en: No, she loves it.
sentences.zh: 不，她很喜欢。

sentences.en: Well, appears to love it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看起来很喜欢。

sentences.en: So, Heath is slightly running with the tide with all this coalition business.
sentences.zh: 所以，希思在这些联合政府的事务上有点顺水推舟。

sentences.en: All his sort of wet Tory moderates, the kind of patrician people that he surrounds himself with, the Willie White Laws and Serene Gilmores and Peter Walkers and people like this,
sentences.zh: 他周围那些温和派保守党人，那些他身边的贵族派人物，比如威利·怀特劳、塞琳·吉尔摩、彼得·沃克之流，

sentences.en: names that will be familiar to some of our older listeners or people who know about British politics in the next 20 years or so.
sentences.zh: 这些名字对于我们一些年长的听众，或者了解未来20年左右英国政治的人来说应该很熟悉。

sentences.en: They love all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢这一套。

sentences.en: Getting together in their national interests, putting aside tribalism, consensus.
sentences.zh: 为了国家利益团结起来，抛弃部落主义，达成共识。

sentences.en: And indeed, the papers love it.
sentences.zh: 而且，报纸确实很喜欢。

sentences.en: The papers are all very be kind about this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 报纸对这件事都非常客气，汤姆。

sentences.en: The Guardian, The Times.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》、《泰晤士报》。

sentences.en: They all say, let's have a coalition, maybe liberal Tory, maybe liberal Labour, maybe Tory Labour, national government in the national intereSt.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，让我们组建联合政府吧，也许是自由党和保守党，也许是自由党和工党，也许是保守党和工党，为了国家利益组建民族政府。

sentences.en: I suppose, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我想也是，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I mean, you're being very sneery about this, but I suppose it's sensible politics on one level because after the previous election, had Thorpe and Heath been able to get together,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你对这件事表现得很不屑，但我觉得从某种层面来看，这是理性的政治，因为在上一次选举后，如果索普和希思能够达成一致，

sentences.en: then there would have been a coalition.
sentences.zh: 那么就会有一个联合政府了。

sentences.en: So, is there a sense in which the Tories are kind of laying out their stall for future coalition partners?
sentences.zh: 所以，保守党是否在某种程度上为未来的联合政府伙伴铺路？

sentences.en: Yes, arguably.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以说有这个意思。

sentences.en: They think that the Liberals will do well again.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自由党会再次表现出色。

sentences.en: But sorry, I never answered you about Mrs. Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我还没回答你关于撒切尔夫人的问题。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher never says a word of complaints about all this.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人对这一切从未有过半句怨言。

sentences.en: Now, of course, later on, she's the sworn foe of compromise and consensus.
sentences.zh: 当然，后来她成了妥协和共识的死敌。

sentences.en: But actually, I said previously she hadn't been a massive star because she hadn't really featured that much in their first election campaign.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我之前说她不是大明星，是因为她在第一次竞选活动中并没有太多表现。

sentences.en: So, does she feature a lot in this one?
sentences.zh: 那么，她在这次竞选中表现突出吗？

sentences.en: In this one, she appears more often than any other Tory frontbencher.
sentences.zh: 在这次竞选中，她出现的频率比任何其他保守党前座议员都要高。

sentences.en: So, she's the breakout star.
sentences.zh: 所以，她是脱颖而出的明星。

sentences.en: She's the breakout star.
sentences.zh: 她是脱颖而出的明星。

sentences.en: So, it's sometimes said that when she became Tory leader a few months later, no one had ever heard of her and she was the sort of the darkest of dark horses.
sentences.zh: 所以有时人们说，当她几个月后成为保守党领袖时，没人听说过她，她是那种最大的黑马。

sentences.en: That's not true at all.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是事实。

sentences.en: She features in their party political broadcasts more than even Heath himself does.
sentences.zh: 她在党派政治广播中出现的次数甚至比希思本人还要多。

sentences.en: Because they think Heath is very abrasive.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为希思太生硬了。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher is maybe more emolient.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人可能更温和一些。

sentences.en: Famous, but yes.
sentences.zh: 很有名，但确实如此。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher would appeal to that crucial dynamic of housewives, which Heath will not appeal to.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人能吸引家庭主妇这一关键群体，而希思则做不到。

sentences.en: And actually, Mrs. Thatcher has a treat for everybody.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，撒切尔夫人给大家准备了一份大礼。

sentences.en: She has an extraordinary bribe.
sentences.zh: 她有一个非同寻常的贿赂手段。

sentences.en: If you're a homeowner in Salisbury, let's say, in Wiltshire, no matter how high inflation and interest rates go, obviously, this is a period of very high inflation,
sentences.zh: 如果你是索尔兹伯里（比如威尔特郡）的房主，无论通货膨胀和利率涨到多高——显然，这是一个高通胀时期——

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher will cap your mortgage rate at 9.5%.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人会将你的抵押贷款利率上限锁定在9.5%。

sentences.en: There is no way it will go higher than that.
sentences.zh: 绝对不会超过这个数字。

sentences.en: So, she's bucking the market.
sentences.zh: 所以，她在对抗市场规律。

sentences.en: She is bucking the market.
sentences.zh: 她确实在对抗市场规律。

sentences.en: It's pure, it's statism gone mad.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是国家主义的疯狂。

sentences.en: Corporatism.
sentences.zh: 法团主义。

sentences.en: It is corporatism.
sentences.zh: 这就是法团主义。

sentences.en: And actually, people who would subsequently become her great admirers on the right are really appalled by this.
sentences.zh: 实际上，那些后来成为她右翼忠实拥护者的人对此感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: They say, this is just the most terrible status bribe for class homeowners.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这简直是对中产阶级房主最糟糕的国家主义贿赂。

sentences.en: But she's a great salesman for it.
sentences.zh: 但她是个出色的推销员。

sentences.en: She goes on TV.
sentences.zh: 她上电视宣传。

sentences.en: She's promising, you know, we'll protect you to value middle class families, trust, struggling to pay the mortgage and all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 她承诺说，你知道，我们会保护你们这些有价值的中产阶级家庭，那些努力支付抵押贷款的人等等。

sentences.en: Hardworking, decent families.
sentences.zh: 勤劳、正派的家庭。

sentences.en: And this is basically the only policy that the Tories have in October 1974.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是保守党在1974年10月唯一的政策。

sentences.en: The rest is all just waffle about coalitions.
sentences.zh: 剩下的全是关于联合政府的废话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He goes to give his first big public meeting in Cardiff.
sentences.zh: 他去卡迪夫参加他的第一场大型公开会议。

sentences.en: This is the new cuddly, jovial, Ted Heath.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个全新的、可爱的、风趣的泰德·希思。

sentences.en: And he speaks very quietly and no one can hear what he's saying because he's obviously been told to tone it down.
sentences.zh: 他说话声音很小，没人能听清他在说什么，因为他显然被告知要收敛一点。

sentences.en: And the first question comes in, somebody says, what will be your first move against inflation, Mr. Heath?
sentences.zh: 第一个问题来了，有人问，希思先生，你对抗通胀的第一步举措是什么？

sentences.en: And he says, to see precisely what the situation is.
sentences.zh: 他说，先看清楚局势究竟如何。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And they say, well, then what will you do?
sentences.zh: 他们又问，那之后你会做什么？

sentences.en: And he says, I'll take the appropriate action.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会采取适当的行动。

sentences.en: Well, that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这真是太精彩了。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: That's masterly.
sentences.zh: 这真是大师级表现。

sentences.en: You've got to give us more than that.
sentences.zh: 你得给我们多说点。

sentences.en: So the mood is very grim.
sentences.zh: 所以气氛非常阴郁。

sentences.en: People on the right are just in absolute misery and despair.
sentences.zh: 右翼人士陷入了绝对的痛苦和绝望之中。

sentences.en: Philip Larkin, Tom, are you a fan of Philip Larkin, the poet?
sentences.zh: 菲利普·拉金，汤姆，你是诗人菲利普·拉金的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, he's basically the most right-wing person in Western Europe at this point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他基本上是当时西欧最右翼的人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And he says, he writes to King's Lamas and he says, we're never going to have another conservative government.
sentences.zh: 他写信给金斯·拉马斯说，我们再也不会有保守党政府了。

sentences.en: There are just going to be a series of Labour governments and then the Russians are going to step in.
sentences.zh: 只会有一连串的工党政府，然后俄国人就会介入。

sentences.en: Amos writes back to him and he says, listen, this is going to be the last free election.
sentences.zh: 阿莫斯回信说，听着，这将是最后一次自由选举。

sentences.en: We'll never be allowed to vote again.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不会被允许投票了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But a lot of people who are kind of affluent, upper middle class kind of people who've done very well are in absolute despair about all this.
sentences.zh: 但是许多富裕的、上中产阶级的人，那些过得很好的人，对这一切感到彻底绝望。

sentences.en: You know, there's a real sense of panic, of kind of moral and political panic among the propertied classes because they can basically,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有产阶级中确实存在一种恐慌，一种道德和政治上的恐慌，因为他们基本上——

sentences.en: they've got their bribe offer from Mrs. Thatcher, but they basically know that the Tories aren't going to get in.
sentences.zh: 他们虽然收到了撒切尔夫人的贿赂承诺，但他们心里清楚保守党不会赢。

sentences.en: So the polls are definitely against the Tories.
sentences.zh: 所以民调绝对对保守党不利。

sentences.en: Oh, very much so.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常不利。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Labour have a lead of about 8 to 10% going into the campaign.
sentences.zh: 所以工党在竞选开始时领先约8到10个百分点。

sentences.en: Because Ted Heath has just regarded as, he's like a football manager who just can't win a game, Tom.
sentences.zh: 因为泰德·希思被视为一个永远赢不了比赛的足球教练，汤姆。

sentences.en: Now you may be wondering, what's happened to our old friends, the Liberals?
sentences.zh: 现在你可能想知道，我们的老朋友自由党怎么样了？

sentences.en: I am wondering about that.
sentences.zh: 我确实在想这个问题。

sentences.en: So the Liberals, the party in the centre, led by Jeremy Thorpe, who will go on to be responsible for the death of a doggone Exmoor and be accused of murder and get off.
sentences.zh: 自由党，这个由杰里米·索普领导的中间派政党，他后来因为埃克斯穆尔的一只狗的死亡而负有责任，并被指控谋杀，最后脱罪。

sentences.en: But anyway, that's all by the by.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，那都是题外话了。

sentences.en: We've done an episode on that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经做过一期关于那个的节目了。

sentences.en: So what does Jeremy Thorpe up to?
sentences.zh: 那么杰里米·索普在忙什么？

sentences.en: And does it involve hovercrafts?
sentences.zh: 这和气垫船有关吗？

sentences.en: It's important to say that whatever the Tories' other failings, they're the only party in this election who have not in some way been involved in a murder plot.
sentences.zh: 必须说明的是，无论保守党还有什么其他失败之处，他们是这次选举中唯一没有以某种方式卷入谋杀阴谋的政党。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, say what you like about Teddy, but he never plotted it as a murder.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不管你怎么评价泰迪，但他从未策划过谋杀。

sentences.en: Either a dog, his ex-lover, or one of his own aides, his secretary.
sentences.zh: 无论是针对狗、他的前情人，还是他自己的助手或秘书。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Jeremy Thorpe, now you would think because he was the breakout star of the first 1974 election, is this his moment?
sentences.zh: 那么杰里米·索普，你可能会想，因为他是1974年第一次选举中脱颖而出的明星，现在是他的时刻吗？

sentences.en: And he thinks that himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己也是这么认为的。

sentences.en: But he has made a terrible mistake, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但他犯了一个严重的错误，汤姆。

sentences.en: He decides to go tour the land.
sentences.zh: 他决定去全国巡回竞选。

sentences.en: I can't even believe I'm going to say it because it sounds so ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信我会说出这种话，因为它听起来太荒谬了。

sentences.en: He's going to tour the land by hovercraft in this election.
sentences.zh: 他打算在这次选举中乘坐气垫船巡回全国。

sentences.en: Is this because all the liberal target seats are on the coast?
sentences.zh: 这是因为所有自由党的目标选区都在沿海吗？

sentences.en: There's a lot on the coast, yeah, on the south coaSt.
sentences.zh: 沿海确实有很多，没错，在南海岸。

sentences.en: I mean, there are quite a lot in the West Country.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在西部地区也有不少。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you get to the heart of the West Country on a hovercraft?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你怎么可能坐着气垫船深入西部腹地呢？

sentences.en: Will you go around the edge, maybe?
sentences.zh: 你会沿着边缘走吗，也许？

sentences.en: Tornwall and Devon?
sentences.zh: 康沃尔和德文郡？

sentences.en: I mean, that's his thinking.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是他的想法。

sentences.en: Up the River Avon.
sentences.zh: 沿着埃文河上去。

sentences.en: But obviously, I mean, Britain, I don't know whether Britain is peculiarly invested in hovercrafts in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 但显然，我是说，英国，我不知道英国是否在70年代对气垫船情有独钟。

sentences.en: Certainly, I remember being at school.
sentences.zh: 当然，我记得我上学的时候。

sentences.en: Very proud of them.
sentences.zh: 对它们非常自豪。

sentences.en: In the sort of late years of the 70s, all the talk was of hovercrafts.
sentences.zh: 在70年代末期，到处都在谈论气垫船。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like Concord.
sentences.zh: 就像协和式飞机一样。

sentences.en: In my mind, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，是的。

sentences.en: Concord, North Sea Oil, the hovercraft.
sentences.zh: 协和式飞机、北海石油、气垫船。

sentences.en: This is the future of the British economy.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国经济的未来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is what Britain will look like.
sentences.zh: 这就是未来的英国面貌。

sentences.en: So Jeremy Thorpe is associating himself with a bright technological future, perhaps a hint of science fiction.
sentences.zh: 所以杰里米·索普将自己与光明的科技未来联系在一起，或许还带有一丝科幻色彩。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it's all glorious and exciting, and maybe people will go around with those hover things on their backs as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切都很辉煌、很令人兴奋，也许人们以后也会背着那种气垫装置到处走。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Holidays in Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 去木星度假。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So how does that pan out?
sentences.zh: 那么结果如何呢？

sentences.en: It goes very badly.
sentences.zh: 结果非常糟糕。

sentences.en: It goes very badly.
sentences.zh: 结果非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So, Tom, the climax of his hovercraft campaign takes place at Sidmouth.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，他气垫船竞选活动的高潮发生在西德茅斯。

sentences.en: And a reporter who's traveling with Thorpe's campaign thinking, you know, could I be writing about the next prime minister?
sentences.zh: 一位随索普竞选团队旅行的记者心想，你知道，我写的是不是下一任首相呢？

sentences.en: He writes as follows.
sentences.zh: 他是这样写的。

sentences.en: The first wave struck just as the craft was turning off the beach to head away to the Isle of Wight.
sentences.zh: 就在气垫船转离海滩准备前往怀特岛时，第一波浪潮袭来了。

sentences.en: I was pulling on one rope just behind the liberal leader when he was nearly swept into the sea by some breakers.
sentences.zh: 我当时正拉着自由党领袖身后的一根绳子，他差点被几道碎浪卷进海里。

sentences.en: So there are photographers there who are capturing this scene as Thorpe and another liberal guy called John Pardo are staggering through the sea with their possessions.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有摄影师拍下了这一幕，索普和另一位名叫约翰·帕多的自由党人带着他们的财物在海中踉跄前行。

sentences.en: So absolutely the image of a dynamic, go-getting future prime minister.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个充满活力、积极进取的未来首相形象。

sentences.en: But the hovercraft actually ends up being completely destroyed by the waves.
sentences.zh: 但气垫船最终被海浪彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: They'd end up abandoning it, Tom, on the beach, on the shingle.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他们最终不得不把它丢弃在海滩的碎石上。

sentences.en: And, of course, everyone then takes photos of this.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都拍下了这一幕。

sentences.en: There's Jeremy Thorpe's Britain.
sentences.zh: 这就是杰里米·索普的英国。

sentences.en: So it's seen as, I mean, it's seen as a metaphor for Britain and for the liberals, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这被视为，我是说，这被视为英国和自由党的隐喻，是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely it is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Other than this, it's an incredibly uneventful campaign.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，这是一场极其平淡的竞选活动。

sentences.en: It rains all the time.
sentences.zh: 一直在下雨。

sentences.en: I mean, it's October, so it's very gloomy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，现在是十月，所以天气非常阴沉。

sentences.en: This is the, what is this?
sentences.zh: 这是，这是什么？

sentences.en: It's the fourth time that Wilson and Heath have faced each other.
sentences.zh: 这是威尔逊和希思第四次交锋。

sentences.en: So it's a bit like one of those FA Cup or World Cup finals or something where the same, you've seen the same teams a thousand times.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像足总杯或世界杯决赛之类的，你已经看过同样的球队一千次了。

sentences.en: It's always nil-nil.
sentences.zh: 总是零比零。

sentences.en: Germany gets Argentina.
sentences.zh: 德国对阵阿根廷。

sentences.en: It's just so depressing.
sentences.zh: 真是太令人沮丧了。

sentences.en: This is how people feel.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们的感受。

sentences.en: Wilson has a pretty comfortable lead.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊拥有相当稳固的领先优势。

sentences.en: Heath's just wittering on about coalitions and national unity and he hasn't got any policies.
sentences.zh: 希思只是在喋喋不休地谈论联盟和国家团结，但他没有任何政策。

sentences.en: Thorpe's falling into the sea.
sentences.zh: 索普掉进海里了。

sentences.en: Yeah, fell into the sea in this hovercraft.
sentences.zh: 是的，坐着气垫船掉进了海里。

sentences.en: The only thing that can possibly stand in Wilson's way, Tom, is Britain's favourite newspaper at the time.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，唯一可能阻碍威尔逊的东西，是当时英国最受欢迎的报纸。

sentences.en: Not necessarily the best-selling, but probably the one that Middle England enjoyed most, which is, of course, Her Majesty's Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 不一定是销量最好的，但很可能是英格兰中产阶级最喜欢的，当然，就是女王陛下的《每日邮报》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the news reaches Wilson headquarters, the Daily Mail had prepared this enormous story on Wilson's finances.
sentences.zh: 因为消息传到威尔逊总部时，《每日邮报》已经准备好了一篇关于威尔逊财务状况的重磅报道。

sentences.en: And actually, Wilson's finances are a little bit mysterious.
sentences.zh: 实际上，威尔逊的财务状况有点神秘。

sentences.en: He'd got all these royalties from a massive and incredibly boring book that he'd written about his 1960s government.
sentences.zh: 他从自己写的一本关于他60年代政府的厚重且极其无聊的书里赚取了所有版税。

sentences.en: And he'd given a lot of these royalties, it seems, to Marcia to spend on school fees for her children.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来他把这些版税中的很大一部分给了玛西娅，让她支付她孩子的学费。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the rest was in a Swiss bank account.
sentences.zh: 剩下的钱都在一个瑞士银行账户里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So spending it on school fees and Swiss bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以把钱花在学费和瑞士银行账户上。

sentences.en: I mean, what would Tony Benn make of that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，托尼·本会怎么看？

sentences.en: Tony Benn would not be impressed at all.
sentences.zh: 托尼·本一点也不会留下好印象。

sentences.en: And the Daily Mail have got this huge story about this, which they're planning to run.
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》掌握了关于此事的重磅新闻，他们正计划刊登。

sentences.en: And the Wilson team are in absolute kind of tenterhooks about it.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊团队对此感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: And then there's all kinds of, they're waiting for the mail to run it one night.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了各种各样的事情，他们都在等《每日邮报》某天晚上刊登出来。

sentences.en: And there's all rumours coming in.
sentences.zh: 各种传言接踵而至。

sentences.en: There's been a bomb scare and mail headquarters.
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》总部收到了炸弹威胁。

sentences.en: So the place has been evacuated.
sentences.zh: 所以那个地方被疏散了。

sentences.en: They're all kind of high level meetings taking place about where they're going to run this story that could completely change the course of the election.
sentences.zh: 他们正在进行各种高层会议，讨论在哪里刊登这篇可能彻底改变选举进程的报道。

sentences.en: And actually, Wilson's lawyer, Lord Goodman, I think it is, wins the day and persuades them not to run it or intimidates them into not running the story.
sentences.zh: 实际上，威尔逊的律师，我想是古德曼勋爵，最终赢得了胜利，说服了他们不要刊登，或者恐吓他们不要刊登这篇报道。

sentences.en: So the next day comes and goes, and they don't run the story about Wilson's finances.
sentences.zh: 所以第二天过去了，他们没有刊登关于威尔逊财务状况的报道。

sentences.en: So as polling day approaches, 10th of October, there's an inevitability, actually, about Wilson's victory.
sentences.zh: 随着投票日10月10日的临近，威尔逊的胜利实际上已经不可避免了。

sentences.en: All the newspapers, by the way, you know, very few of the newspapers want him to win.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，所有的报纸，你知道，很少有报纸希望他赢。

sentences.en: The Guardian, you know, the Guardian wants to win.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》，你知道，《卫报》希望他赢。

sentences.en: The Liberals.
sentences.zh: 自由党。

sentences.en: Guardian loves the hovercraft business.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》喜欢气垫船那件事。

sentences.en: The Times wants a Tory-Liberal coalition.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》想要一个保守党与自由党的联合政府。

sentences.en: The Mail wants a Tory-Liberal coalition.
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》想要一个保守党与自由党的联合政府。

sentences.en: So the polling day comes, Thursday, the 10th of October, pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 投票日到了，10月10日星期四，大雨倾盆。

sentences.en: Wilson's aides just obviously spend all the time bickering among themselves.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊的助手们显然整天都在互相争吵。

sentences.en: Marcia has got a load of sedatives, which she's washing down with brandy.
sentences.zh: 玛西娅拿了一堆镇静剂，正用白兰地送服。

sentences.en: So she's joined in the drinking.
sentences.zh: 所以她也加入了喝酒的行列。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they sit up.
sentences.zh: 他们坐着等待。

sentences.en: And at first, it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 起初，情况很棒。

sentences.en: The BBC say they're going to get 150 seat majority, Wilson and co.
sentences.zh: BBC说威尔逊及其团队将获得150个席位的多数优势。

sentences.en: But then as the night goes on, that majority gets whittled down and down and down.
sentences.zh: 但随着夜色渐深，多数优势被一点一点地削减。

sentences.en: And he does end up with the majority, Tom, but of just three seats.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他最终确实获得了多数席位，但只有三个席位。

sentences.en: So that's what, only seven or eight more than he'd had in the previous election?
sentences.zh: 所以那是什么，只比他上次选举时多了七八个席位？

sentences.en: Than he started with, yeah.
sentences.zh: 比他开始时多，是的。

sentences.en: So actually, Labour's vote has fallen since February.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，工党的得票率自二月以来有所下降。

sentences.en: The Tory vote had fallen even more.
sentences.zh: 保守党的得票率下降得更多。

sentences.en: It's actually their worst performance since 1945 in number of votes.
sentences.zh: 按票数计算，这实际上是他们自1945年以来的最差表现。

sentences.en: And votes share the Tory performance was terrible, 36%, which is, I think, their worst ever at that point.
sentences.zh: 而在得票份额方面，保守党的表现非常糟糕，只有36%，我认为这是他们当时有史以来的最差成绩。

sentences.en: But what wouldn't Rishi Sunak give for those figures now?
sentences.zh: 但里希·苏纳克现在会多么渴望得到这些数据啊？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a fair point.
sentences.zh: 说得有道理。

sentences.en: So Heath is done.
sentences.zh: 所以希思完了。

sentences.en: We'll come on to Heath after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息过后我们再谈希思。

sentences.en: Just before we go into the break, you'll be pleased to hear that Wilson celebrates in a ludicrously disorganized and chaotic way.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，你会很高兴听到威尔逊以一种极其混乱和无组织的方式庆祝胜利。

sentences.en: I'd be disappointed if he didn't.
sentences.zh: 如果他不这样做，我反而会感到失望。

sentences.en: So they spend the evening arguing about who's going to go to the victory party.
sentences.zh: 所以他们整个晚上都在争论谁去参加庆功宴。

sentences.en: There's an argument about one of his most faithful aides.
sentences.zh: 关于他最忠诚的一位助手还有一场争论。

sentences.en: He's got Albert Murray, who basically carries his bag for him.
sentences.zh: 他有阿尔伯特·默里，基本上是帮他拎包的人。

sentences.en: Marcia says he's not allowed in.
sentences.zh: 玛西娅说他不准进去。

sentences.en: So the others have just taken a dislike to him.
sentences.zh: 所以其他人只是对他产生了反感。

sentences.en: So the others boycott the boycott his victory party because Albert's not allowed him.
sentences.zh: 所以其他人抵制了他的庆功宴，因为阿尔伯特不被允许参加。

sentences.en: There's a great deal of rage.
sentences.zh: 现场非常愤怒。

sentences.en: They go off to a different hotel, I think, to watch the telly.
sentences.zh: 我想他们去了另一家酒店看电视。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then the next day, there's a big argument about who's going to be allowed on the flight home to London.
sentences.zh: 第二天，关于谁能获准搭乘航班回伦敦又发生了一场大争论。

sentences.en: They finally get to London to go to Transport House, Labour Party headquarters for their victory celebration.
sentences.zh: 他们终于到达伦敦，前往工党总部运输大厦参加他们的胜利庆典。

sentences.en: There is a bomb scare.
sentences.zh: 结果又收到了炸弹威胁。

sentences.en: So again, that issue of the IRA hangs over the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，爱尔兰共和军的问题再次笼罩着整个事件。

sentences.en: So there's a bomb scare.
sentences.zh: 所以又是一次炸弹威胁。

sentences.en: The whole place has to be evacuated.
sentences.zh: 整个地方不得不被疏散。

sentences.en: And then the really, really big news.
sentences.zh: 然后是真正的大新闻。

sentences.en: That day, they've got back to London.
sentences.zh: 那天，他们回到了伦敦。

sentences.en: They now have the tiny majority and they can look into turning the nation's fortunes around.
sentences.zh: 他们现在拥有微弱的多数席位，可以着手扭转国家的命运了。

sentences.en: And Bernard Donoghue, the policy chief of Harold Wilson, is at number 10.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·威尔逊的政策主管伯纳德·多诺霍当时在唐宁街10号。

sentences.en: And he's actually going to go off for the weekend and kind of clear his mind and think about what they need to do to sort things out.
sentences.zh: 他本来打算周末出去走走，清空一下思绪，思考一下他们需要做些什么来解决问题。

sentences.en: And just before he does, one of Wilson's civil servants comes in and says to him,
sentences.zh: 就在他出发前，威尔逊的一名公务员走进来对他说：

sentences.en: I've got some news.
sentences.zh: 我有个消息。

sentences.en: There's been a big breakthrough in the lunch negotiations.
sentences.zh: 午餐谈判取得了重大突破。

sentences.en: And the big breakthrough is everybody is now banned from having lunch in number 10 to sort it all out.
sentences.zh: 而所谓的重大突破就是，现在禁止所有人在唐宁街10号吃午餐，以解决所有问题。

sentences.en: And Donoghue writes in his diary that evening, I hope Harold gets a minute to think about the country's economy in between acting as a messenger for Marcia's hostilities.

sentences.zh: 他正处于政治胜利的时刻，却把时间花在这些关于谁能在唐宁街10号吃午餐的琐碎小事上，充当传话筒。
