sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History for the final segment of our four-part epic on the single year of 1974 in Britain.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《历史的余味》，这是我们关于英国1974年这一单一年份的四集史诗系列的最后一集。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we began this episode with a bombing by the IRA of a pub.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们这一集开头讲的是爱尔兰共和军（IRA）对一家酒吧的爆炸袭击。

sentences.en: And we're going to begin this half with the bombing of another pub by the IRA.
sentences.zh: 而这一半的开头，我们将讲述爱尔兰共和军对另一家酒吧的爆炸袭击。

sentences.en: And this was in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 这次是在伯明翰。

sentences.en: It's very vivid in my imagination because it features in Jonathan Coe's brilliant novel.
sentences.zh: 我的脑海里对此印象非常深刻，因为它出现在乔纳森·科伊那部精彩的小说中。

sentences.en: In fact, growing up in Birmingham in the 70s, The Rotter's Club.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在70年代的伯明翰长大，那部小说叫《腐败俱乐部》。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是它。

sentences.en: The hero's sister's boyfriend dies in it.
sentences.zh: 主角妹妹的男朋友在爆炸中丧生了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a brilliant book and a very affecting moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一本精彩的书，也是一个非常令人感伤的时刻。

sentences.en: So this is six weeks after the Guildford bombing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是吉尔福德爆炸案发生六周后。

sentences.en: So it's about five weeks after the general election.
sentences.zh: 距离大选大约五周。

sentences.en: And it's a Thursday in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 那是一个星期四，在伯明翰。

sentences.en: It's payday in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 那是伯明翰的发薪日。

sentences.en: So the pubs are crowded.
sentences.zh: 所以酒吧里挤满了人。

sentences.en: There's a basement pub called the Tavern in the Town, not far from New Street Station.
sentences.zh: 有一家叫“城中酒馆”的地下酒吧，离新街车站不远。

sentences.en: So if those people are familiar with the centre of Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 如果大家熟悉伯明翰市中心的话。

sentences.en: And just after about 8.15, the people in that pub, they hear a kind of muffled thump.
sentences.zh: 大约8点15分刚过，酒吧里的人听到了一声闷响。

sentences.en: And they don't know it.
sentences.zh: 他们当时并不知道。

sentences.en: But a bomb has just gone off at the bottom of the Rotunda in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 但一枚炸弹刚刚在伯明翰圆厅大厦底部爆炸了。

sentences.en: The pub at the bottom of Rotunda, which is just a few minutes walk away.
sentences.zh: 圆厅大厦底部的酒吧，距离这里只有几分钟的步行路程。

sentences.en: And exactly 10 minutes after that.
sentences.zh: 就在那之后整整10分钟。

sentences.en: So there's crowds gathering outside this pub now as people are moving down the street.
sentences.zh: 当时人们正沿着街道走，酒吧外已经聚集了人群。

sentences.en: A bomb goes off in the tavern in the town as well.
sentences.zh: “城中酒馆”也发生了一起爆炸。

sentences.en: So it's the second bombing of the night.
sentences.zh: 所以这是当晚的第二次爆炸。

sentences.en: And if you read the descriptions in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 如果你读过报纸上的描述。

sentences.en: The descriptions are horrific.
sentences.zh: 那些描述非常恐怖。

sentences.en: So a fireman recall seeing a torso with no arms or legs and a spongy mess where its head had been.
sentences.zh: 一位消防员回忆说，看到一具没有胳膊和腿的躯干，头部的位置是一团海绵状的烂肉。

sentences.en: The torso was not only wriggling.
sentences.zh: 那具躯干不仅在蠕动。

sentences.en: It was also through the spongy mess screaming.
sentences.zh: 而且那团海绵状的烂肉还在尖叫。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so horrible.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the fireman asked the TV crews to film some of these scenes.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以消防员要求电视摄制组拍摄其中一些场景。

sentences.en: And the TV crews refused because they said they were too horrific.
sentences.zh: 但摄制组拒绝了，因为他们说场面太恐怖了。

sentences.en: 21 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 21人遇难。

sentences.en: Almost 200 injured, some of them very badly.
sentences.zh: 近200人受伤，其中一些伤势非常严重。

sentences.en: There was actually a third bomb in a wine bar.
sentences.zh: 实际上还有第三枚炸弹在一家红酒吧里。

sentences.en: So basically what had happened is the IRA had put a bomb in the first pub at the bottom of the Rotunda.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上发生的情况是，爱尔兰共和军在圆厅大厦底部的第一家酒吧放了一枚炸弹。

sentences.en: Then they had planned it so that as people fled, a second bomb in a pub just down the street would catch them.
sentences.zh: 然后他们计划好，当人们逃离时，街头另一家酒吧的第二枚炸弹会炸中他们。

sentences.en: They claimed they had telephoned warnings, but they did so with so little time before the pub bombs went off.
sentences.zh: 他们声称打过警告电话，但距离酒吧爆炸的时间太短了。

sentences.en: There was no way that the police could act or the pubs could be evacuated.
sentences.zh: 警方根本来不及采取行动，酒吧也无法及时疏散。

sentences.en: And because it comes so soon after the Guildford bombing, I think there's a real sense of shock, of trauma, particularly in the city of Birmingham, in the aftermath of all this.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它发生在吉尔福德爆炸案之后不久，我认为在这一切发生后，伯明翰市有一种强烈的震惊和创伤感。

sentences.en: There was talk at the time, briefly, that this would spark, you know, sort of sectarian or sort of backlash politics in Britain itself.
sentences.zh: 当时曾短暂地有过一种说法，认为这会在英国本土引发宗派主义或某种反弹政治。

sentences.en: So what, anti-Irish pogroms?
sentences.zh: 你是说反爱尔兰的大屠杀吗？

sentences.en: Anti-Irish, exactly.
sentences.zh: 反爱尔兰，没错。

sentences.en: So there were a few isolated incidents.
sentences.zh: 所以确实发生了一些孤立的事件。

sentences.en: So there's petrol bombs that are thrown at an Irish pub in West London.
sentences.zh: 比如有人向伦敦西区的一家爱尔兰酒吧投掷汽油弹。

sentences.en: There are talks about people attacking Irish community centres and things.
sentences.zh: 还有关于人们袭击爱尔兰社区中心之类的传言。

sentences.en: But actually, by and large, it doesn't really come to very much.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，总的来说，并没有闹出太大的动静。

sentences.en: The government, in the aftermath, passed a Prevention of Terrorism Act.
sentences.zh: 事后，政府通过了《防止恐怖主义法案》。

sentences.en: So that allowed people to be held for questioning for seven days, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，这允许将嫌疑人扣留审讯七天。

sentences.en: But actually, looking at it now, I think the striking thing is actually how muted...
sentences.zh: 但现在回过头来看，我认为最引人注目的是，实际上它是多么的平淡……

sentences.en: Except that, as with Guildford, the police are looking to finger people they can blame.
sentences.zh: 除了像吉尔福德案一样，警方急于找人背锅。

sentences.en: And there's, again, there's another terrible miscarriage of justice, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且，又是一起可怕的司法不公，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Birmingham Six.
sentences.zh: 是的，“伯明翰六人组”。

sentences.en: So that's six men.
sentences.zh: 那是六名男子。

sentences.en: They're Irishmen who'd lived in Birmingham since the 60s.
sentences.zh: 他们是从60年代起就住在伯明翰的爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: They're arrested.
sentences.zh: 他们被捕了。

sentences.en: Confessions are beaten out of them.
sentences.zh: 他们被严刑逼供，被迫认罪。

sentences.en: They were in prison until 1991, until the conviction was overturned.
sentences.zh: 他们一直被关在监狱里直到1991年，直到定罪被推翻。

sentences.en: So this is a grim background to the start of Wilson's...
sentences.zh: 所以这就是威尔逊执政初期的严峻背景……

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 这是第几任？

sentences.en: Now I'm losing track.
sentences.zh: 我现在有点记不清了。

sentences.en: His fourth term?
sentences.zh: 他的第四个任期？

sentences.en: His third term?
sentences.zh: 他的第三个任期？

sentences.en: It depends how you measure it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你怎么算，汤姆。

sentences.en: But it's a sort of continuation.
sentences.zh: 但这算是一种延续。

sentences.en: He's won four elections.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了四次大选。

sentences.en: He's won four elections out of five.
sentences.zh: 他五次大选中赢了四次。

sentences.en: So whatever you say about Harold Wilson, he's a very cunning operator.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你怎么评价哈罗德·威尔逊，他都是一个非常狡猾的操盘手。

sentences.en: He's very good at elections.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长选举。

sentences.en: Even 1970, you know, which he lost, he actually did well to come as...
sentences.zh: 即使是1970年那次，你知道，虽然他输了，但他能取得那样的成绩其实已经很不错了……

sentences.en: I would argue, given his record in government, I think he actually did well to come within a...
sentences.zh: 我认为，考虑到他的执政记录，他能取得那样的成绩其实已经很不错了……

sentences.en: You know, to have a chance of winning it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，能有机会获胜。

sentences.en: So Wilson appeals to people who want a quiet life.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔逊吸引的是那些想要过安稳生活的人。

sentences.en: I think the key to Wilson is that people in Britain, I think in the 60s and 70s, they were tired.
sentences.zh: 我认为威尔逊的关键在于，英国人在60和70年代感到疲惫。

sentences.en: They were very anxious about change.
sentences.zh: 他们对变革感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: They were conscious of no longer being top nation.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到自己不再是世界顶尖国家了。

sentences.en: And I think in some part of their minds, a lot of people didn't know that they were facing a very difficult transformation as the industries on which they relied, coal,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在他们潜意识的某个角落，很多人并没有意识到他们正面临着一场极其艰难的转型，因为他们所依赖的产业，煤炭、

sentences.en: shipbuilding, steel, all those kinds of things, that they were clearly struggling.
sentences.zh: 造船、钢铁，所有这些行业，显然都在挣扎。

sentences.en: But they didn't really want to face it.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不想真正面对这个问题。

sentences.en: Actually, the person we've mentioned a lot who writes this diary, Bernard Donoghue, Wilson's policy chief, is brilliant on all this in his diaries and in his memoirs, saying,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们提到过很多次的写日记的人，威尔逊的政策主管伯纳德·多诺霍，在他的日记和回忆录中对这一切的描述非常精彩，他说，

sentences.en: you know, we knew that change would have to come.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们知道变革终将到来。

sentences.en: But actually, we were benefiting electorally from people who wanted to put that off, right?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们从那些想要推迟变革的人身上获得了选举红利，对吧？

sentences.en: And Wilson's political persona, I think, is one of very, very small C conservatism by this point.
sentences.zh: 而威尔逊的政治形象，我认为到这个时候已经是非常非常保守的了。

sentences.en: It's basically, let's not frighten the horses, no conflicts with the unions, nothing that will lead to any kind of public controversy, just steady as she goes.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，别惊动了马匹，不要与工会发生冲突，不要做任何会导致公众争议的事情，一切照旧就好。

sentences.en: And actually, the orderly management of decline, to some extent, Tom.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，汤姆，这其实就是对衰落的有序管理。

sentences.en: So, I suppose there are two radical solutions to this crisis, both of which involve a pretty dramatic restructuring of the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想对于这场危机有两种激进的解决方案，两者都涉及对经济进行相当剧烈的重组。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The first would be the one proposed by Tony Benn, that you become almost a siege economy.
sentences.zh: 第一个是托尼·本恩提出的，即让你变成一个几乎封闭的堡垒经济。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That you thumb your nose at the power of international capital.
sentences.zh: 即对国际资本的力量嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the other is the radical turn that the British economy does end up taking, most famously with Mrs. Thatcher, but also, of course, as you brilliantly point out in your book,
sentences.zh: 另一个是英国经济最终采取的激进转向，最著名的是撒切尔夫人时期，但当然，正如你在书中精彩指出的那样，

sentences.en: before that with Dennis Healy.
sentences.zh: 在那之前还有丹尼斯·希利。

sentences.en: And is there a sense in the wake of the election that these are really the two alternatives, that just going with the status quo is going to be inadequate?
sentences.zh: 在大选之后，是否有一种感觉，认为这确实是仅有的两种选择，而仅仅维持现状是不够的？

sentences.en: No, not initially, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不，起初并不是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, on the Tony Benn thing, whatever else you say about Tony Benn, he had a very coherent and thought-through approach to dealing with the problem that Britain was facing,
sentences.zh: 关于托尼·本恩的那一套，无论你怎么评价他，他对于解决英国面临的问题确实有一套非常连贯且深思熟虑的方法，

sentences.en: which was, as you say, a siege economy, protectionism, rebuild British industry behind a kind of tariff wall.
sentences.zh: 也就是你说的，堡垒经济、保护主义，在关税壁垒的保护下重建英国工业。

sentences.en: Because the contrast with Wilson, in a way, it seems that all this stuff about dinners and whatever with Marcia, it's a displacement exercise.
sentences.zh: 因为与威尔逊相比，在某种程度上，所有关于和玛西娅共进晚餐之类的传闻，似乎只是一种转移注意力的手段。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to have to engage with it.
sentences.zh: 他不想去面对这些问题。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 同意。

sentences.en: Whereas Ben really is engaging with it.
sentences.zh: 而本恩确实是在积极应对。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I totally agree, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, in fact, the people who are working on policy, the backroom boys, as it were, they are all boys, except for Marcia, in number 10, say again and again in this period, 1974,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上，那些负责政策的人，也就是所谓的幕后操盘手——他们全是男的，除了玛西娅——在1974年、

sentences.en: 1975, 1976, he doesn't read the papers.
sentences.zh: 1975年、1976年这段时间里，一次又一次地说，他不看报纸。

sentences.en: He doesn't engage.
sentences.zh: 他不参与其中。

sentences.en: Inflation is heading towards 30%, but he doesn't really want to do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀率正朝着30%迈进，但他并不想对此做任何事。

sentences.en: And they're really frustrated by it, actually.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And so, what happens in the months immediately after the election?
sentences.zh: 那么，大选后的几个月里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Is there any sense of an election bounce?
sentences.zh: 有任何选举后的反弹迹象吗？

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: It's actually a sort of, whatever, they're letting the air out of the balloon.
sentences.zh: 实际上这更像是一种……怎么说呢，他们在给气球放气。

sentences.en: Yeah, the air out of a balloon.
sentences.zh: 是的，给气球放气。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有。

sentences.en: So, actually, by the end of October, Dennis Healy, who had thrown a lot of money around to try and win the election, meets his colleagues and actually says to them,
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上到了10月底，为了赢得大选而挥霍了大量资金的丹尼斯·希利，在会见同事时竟然对他们说，

sentences.en: and do you know what, actually, all our projections were too optimistic.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，其实我们所有的预测都太乐观了。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise.
sentences.zh: 不出所料。

sentences.en: We're going to be borrowing probably twice as much money as we thought we would, and that's going to rise three times as much in a year or so.
sentences.zh: 我们借的钱可能比预想的要多一倍，而且一年左右的时间里还会增加三倍。

sentences.en: So, inflation is totally out of control now.
sentences.zh: 所以，通货膨胀现在完全失控了。

sentences.en: It's well into 20%.
sentences.zh: 已经远超20%了。

sentences.en: The threshold payments, which we mentioned in the very first episode of this series, they've now been triggered, Tom, giving you an automatic pay rise because of inflation.
sentences.zh: 我们在本系列第一集提到的门槛支付条款，现在已经被触发了，汤姆，因为通货膨胀，这会自动给你加薪。

sentences.en: They've been triggered 11 times.
sentences.zh: 它们已经被触发了11次。

sentences.en: So, adding to the kind of inflationary spiral.
sentences.zh: 所以，这加剧了通货膨胀的螺旋式上升。

sentences.en: And in November, all the Wilson government get together, well, the Wilson cabinet, they get together at Chequers.
sentences.zh: 11月，整个威尔逊政府聚在一起，好吧，是威尔逊内阁，他们在契克斯庄园聚会。

sentences.en: So, this is the official residence, country residence of the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 这是首相的官方乡村官邸。

sentences.en: They're unbelievably pessimistic about the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们对经济持有一种难以置信的悲观态度。

sentences.en: And the most famous line from this meeting, a very famous line, which is a great epitaph for the 70s, comes from very much a friend of the rest is history, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这次会议中最著名的一句话，一句非常著名的话，也是对70年代最好的墓志铭，出自“余下的历史”节目的老朋友汤姆之口。

sentences.en: James Callaghan, your great hero, later prime minister.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·卡拉汉，你心目中的大英雄，后来的首相。

sentences.en: They say, what do you think, Jim?
sentences.zh: 他们问：吉姆，你怎么看？

sentences.en: And Jim says, well, when I'm shaving in the morning, I say to myself that if we're a young man, I'd emigrate.
sentences.zh: 吉姆回答说：嗯，我每天早上刮胡子的时候，都会对自己说，如果我还年轻，我一定会移民。

sentences.en: And obviously, everybody laughs, but he's only half joking because he says to them in that meeting, if we carry on as we are,
sentences.zh: 显然，大家都笑了，但他其实只开了半个玩笑，因为他在那次会议上对他们说，如果我们继续这样下去，

sentences.en: we will be stripped of our seat on the UN Security Council.
sentences.zh: 我们将失去在联合国安理会的席位。

sentences.en: Then he goes on to say, nothing in these papers makes me believe anything to the contrary, but I haven't got any solution.
sentences.zh: 接着他又说，这些文件里没有任何内容让我相信情况会有所好转，但我也没有任何解决办法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which obviously is slightly sub-ideal.
sentences.zh: 这显然有点不太理想。

sentences.en: And actually, the thing about emigrating, loads of people are emigrating.
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于移民这件事，确实有很多人正在移民。

sentences.en: So, David Bowie's off, isn't he, to New York?
sentences.zh: 大卫·鲍伊也走了，对吧？去了纽约？

sentences.en: New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约。

sentences.en: The Stones are still in the south of France, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想滚石乐队应该还在法国南部。

sentences.en: Roger Moore, Tom?
sentences.zh: 罗杰·摩尔呢，汤姆？

sentences.en: James Bond's left.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·邦德也离开了。

sentences.en: Where does he go?
sentences.zh: 他去哪儿了？

sentences.en: So, Roger Moore, I think, went in about 73.
sentences.zh: 罗杰·摩尔大概是在73年左右离开的。

sentences.en: But actually, the Bond films themselves go because Moonraker ends up being filmed in France at the end of the 70s for tax reasons.
sentences.zh: 其实连邦德系列电影本身也离开了，因为70年代末，《太空城》最终为了避税是在法国拍摄的。

sentences.en: God, the humiliation.
sentences.zh: 天哪，真是丢人。

sentences.en: But also, lots of young people go, so many, in fact, that for the first time in 1974, New Zealand bring in controls to stop so many British people moving to New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多年轻人离开，事实上人数之多，以至于1974年新西兰首次实施了管控，以阻止大量英国人移居新西兰。

sentences.en: And Australia follows suit in 1975.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚也在1975年效仿了这一做法。

sentences.en: So, this is unprecedented, that they are closing their doors.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们开始关上大门，这在以前是前所未有的。

sentences.en: I'll tell you some English tourists who are in Australia in the latter half, after the election, is the England cricket team.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，在选举后的下半年，有一群英国游客在澳大利亚，那就是英格兰板球队。

sentences.en: I knew this was coming.
sentences.zh: 我就知道会提到这个。

sentences.en: Playing against Rodney Marsh, the Australian wicketkeeper, not the Manchester City striker.
sentences.zh: 他们对阵的是澳大利亚的守门员罗德尼·马什，不是那个曼城的前锋。

sentences.en: A poorly behaved Manchester City striker from the last episode.
sentences.zh: 就是上一集里提到的那个表现不佳的曼城前锋。

sentences.en: And they get absolutely torn to pieces by Dennis Lilley and Geoff Thompson, the most ferocious fast bowlers.
sentences.zh: 结果他们被丹尼斯·利利和杰夫·汤姆森这两位最凶猛的快球手打得落花流水。

sentences.en: And at one point, the abdominal protector, which is a David Lloyd, England batsman, he almost becomes a eunuch, gets cracked in two.
sentences.zh: 有一次，英格兰击球手大卫·劳埃德的护裆——他差点就成了太监——被直接击成了两半。

sentences.en: And there, I'm afraid, is a metaphor, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 恐怕这就是一个隐喻，对吧？

sentences.en: There is a metaphor, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实是个隐喻，没错。

sentences.en: So, 1975, would you believe, so the year after the election, was the first year since records began that Britain's population fell because so many people were emigrating.
sentences.zh: 所以，你敢信吗？1975年，也就是选举后的第二年，是自记录开始以来英国人口首次出现下降，因为移民的人实在太多了。

sentences.en: So, there is a solution to the immigration crisis.
sentences.zh: 所以，移民危机是有解决办法的。

sentences.en: What, punch our economy into the abyss?
sentences.zh: 什么？把我们的经济打入深渊吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Conservatives could totally crash the economy.
sentences.zh: 没错，保守党完全可以搞垮经济。

sentences.en: Well, let us end with the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们以保守党作为结尾。

sentences.en: So, just on Wilson, just before Christmas, one of Wilson's aides gave him a paper saying, we are facing an economic Armageddon.
sentences.zh: 关于威尔逊，就在圣诞节前，他的一位助手递给他一份文件，说我们正面临经济上的世界末日。

sentences.en: As it turned out, the real reckoning was delayed until just after he left office in 1976.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，真正的清算被推迟到了他1976年离任之后。

sentences.en: So, he leaves office in the spring of 1976, absolutely knackered, worn out, massive bags under his eyes, very hangdog.
sentences.zh: 他在1976年春天离任时，已经彻底精疲力竭，眼袋深重，看起来非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And almost immediately afterwards, there is a huge run on the pound and Britain has to seek a humiliating world record bailout international monetary fund, which later becomes,
sentences.zh: 几乎就在他离任后不久，英镑就遭遇了巨大的抛售，英国不得不寻求国际货币基金组织创纪录的羞辱性救助，这后来成了，

sentences.en: of course, an item on the Thatterite charge sheet against the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是撒切尔主义者指责70年代的一项罪状。

sentences.en: That and the Winter of Discontent.
sentences.zh: 还有“不满之冬”。

sentences.en: Which follows later in the decade.
sentences.zh: 那是在十年后期发生的。

sentences.en: When there's kind of non-stop strikes and gravediggers go on strike and things.
sentences.zh: 当时罢工不断，连掘墓人都罢工了之类的。

sentences.en: So, just before we do come to what happens to Edward Heath, just the state of the economy, because people say now that the country is in a worse mess than it's ever been in.
sentences.zh: 在我们谈到爱德华·希思的遭遇之前，先说说当时的经济状况，因为现在人们常说国家正处于有史以来最糟糕的境地。

sentences.en: It's not as bad, at least it doesn't seem as bad, as it was back then.
sentences.zh: 至少看起来，并没有当时那么糟糕。

sentences.en: Is it actually the case the economy isn't quite as bad as we've been making it out to sound?
sentences.zh: 现在的经济真的像我们描述的那么差吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's as bad as now as it was in the 70s by any means.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在的经济无论如何都比不上70年代那么糟糕。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不至于。

sentences.en: I think the economy is obviously far from perfect now, but we don't have inflation at 27%.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在的经济显然远非完美，但我们并没有27%的通货膨胀率。

sentences.en: Economies fluctuate, Tom.
sentences.zh: 经济总是波动的，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, good times, bad times, stock markets rise and fall.
sentences.zh: 有好时光，也有坏时光，股市有涨有跌。

sentences.en: To some degree, standing back, you might say a little bit of this is surface froth, right?
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上退一步看，你可能会说这其中有一点是表面的泡沫，对吧？

sentences.en: But what's gone on with Britain between the 1950s and the 1980s is much more than surface froth.
sentences.zh: 但英国在1950年代到1980年代之间发生的事情，远不止是表面的泡沫。

sentences.en: It's a massive structural change.
sentences.zh: 那是一场巨大的结构性变革。

sentences.en: So, it's a process of kind of de-industrialization, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个去工业化的过程，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, it absolutely is de-industrialization.
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是去工业化。

sentences.en: So, first into industry and first out.
sentences.zh: 所以，最先进入工业化，也最先退出。

sentences.en: And what's happening, I think, in the 70s is that the Wilson government and Callaghan government, like the Heath government before it, are trying to insulate,
sentences.zh: 我认为70年代发生的事情是，威尔逊政府和卡拉汉政府，就像之前的希思政府一样，都在试图保护，

sentences.en: for completely humane and understandable reasons, trying to insulate a lot of working people from the consequences of that transformation.
sentences.zh: 出于完全人道和可以理解的原因，试图让许多劳动人民免受这种转型带来的后果。

sentences.en: So, you know, when you read the papers and things, they will discuss a car factory in Scotland or something, and they will say, well, we just have to put money into it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当你读报纸的时候，他们会讨论苏格兰的一家汽车工厂什么的，他们会说，好吧，我们必须投入资金。

sentences.en: We have to keep it going because if we let it fold, thousands of people will lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们必须维持它的运转，因为如果我们让它倒闭，成千上万的人就会失业。

sentences.en: The effect on the local community will be terrible.
sentences.zh: 这对当地社区的影响将是可怕的。

sentences.en: We don't want to be a government that allows that to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们不想成为一个允许这种情况发生的政府。

sentences.en: We'll find the money.
sentences.zh: 我们会筹集资金的。

sentences.en: And the danger with doing that, of course, is you just put off the evil day and you make it worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样做的危险在于，你只是推迟了痛苦的到来，反而让情况变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: And I think there was a definite sense by the end of the 70s, and this is very palpable in the memoirs and the diaries of people in the Labour government, not the Tories,
sentences.zh: 我认为到70年代末，有一种明确的感觉，这在工党政府成员的回忆录和日记中非常明显，不是托利党，

sentences.en: but the Labour government.
sentences.zh: 而是工党政府。

sentences.en: There was a sense, we actually can't keep doing this forever.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉是：我们真的不能永远这样下去了。

sentences.en: You know, something is going to have to change at some point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，总有一天会有所改变。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I think the economy, the picture was worse in the 70s because people knew that what would follow would be so, would be brutal, brutal, exactly,
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我认为70年代的经济状况更糟，因为人们知道接下来会发生的事情将是残酷的，非常残酷，确实如此，

sentences.en: which I don't think we have now.
sentences.zh: 而我认为我们现在还没有到那种地步。

sentences.en: Well, unless they are siding with the Benite diagnosis and the Benite prescription.
sentences.zh: 除非他们支持贝恩派的诊断和处方。

sentences.en: But even the Benite prescription, you see, the Benite prescription is an interesting, really interesting one because when it was modelled, when people said, well,
sentences.zh: 但即使是贝恩派的处方，你看，贝恩派的处方是一个非常有趣的例子，因为当它被建模时，当人们说，好吧，

sentences.en: what would actually happen if we said sod you to the IMF and the World Bank and whatnot?
sentences.zh: 如果我们对国际货币基金组织和世界银行之类的机构说“去你的”，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And we sealed ourselves off from the world economy to some extent.
sentences.zh: 如果我们某种程度上将自己与世界经济隔绝开来。

sentences.en: Actually, what would happen would be probably very, very high inflation.
sentences.zh: 实际上，可能会发生非常非常高的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And even though lots of people would still be in work,
sentences.zh: 即使很多人仍然有工作，

sentences.en: there would probably be a massive drop in a lot of people's living standards because imports would be so expensive because everybody else would put up trade barriers against Britain.
sentences.zh: 很多人的生活水平也可能会大幅下降，因为进口商品会变得非常昂贵，而且其他人会对英国设置贸易壁垒。

sentences.en: So the Benite solution was by no means a panacea.
sentences.zh: 所以贝恩派的方案绝不是万灵药。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, I don't think it was a panacea because I don't think it would have worked.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，我不认为它是万灵药，因为我不认为它会奏效。

sentences.en: But, I mean, the idea that you could just go on as you were, just finding bailouts all the time,
sentences.zh: 但是，那种认为你可以继续维持现状，一直寻找救助的想法，

sentences.en: I don't think anybody thought that in the long run that would possibly be a solution.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有人会认为从长远来看这可能是一个解决方案。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's just finish this by looking at what happens with the Tories.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们以保守党的情况来结束这个话题。

sentences.en: Because, of course, the political figure who emerges from this, she's been a bit part player really so far, but she will become the dominant figure in the 80s, is Mrs. Thatcher,
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，从这场混乱中脱颖而出的政治人物，虽然她之前只是个小角色，但她将成为80年代的主导人物，那就是撒切尔夫人，

sentences.en: who ends up replacing Edward Heath as leader.
sentences.zh: 她最终取代了爱德华·希思成为领导人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Although she shouldn't have done, Tom.
sentences.zh: 虽然她本不该如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's the extraordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是最不可思议的事情。

sentences.en: So, first of all, Heath has now loSt. He's lost three out of four elections, and he's lost two in a row in a single year.
sentences.zh: 首先，希思现在输了。他在四次选举中输了三次，而且在一年内连续输了两次。

sentences.en: So he really, I mean, he has to go.
sentences.zh: 所以他真的，我的意思是，他必须走人。

sentences.en: I don't think it's at all unreasonable to think that he would want to go.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他想离开的想法有什么不合理的。

sentences.en: But he refuses to go.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝离开。

sentences.en: Very Ted Heath behaviour.
sentences.zh: 非常典型的泰德·希思式的行为。

sentences.en: He's sulky.
sentences.zh: 他闷闷不乐。

sentences.en: He's sort of sullen.
sentences.zh: 他有点阴沉。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to talk to anybody.
sentences.zh: 他不想和任何人说话。

sentences.en: But it strikes him as outrageous that people would suggest that he, I mean, he basically doesn't even want to admit that he's loSt.
sentences.zh: 但让他觉得离谱的是，竟然有人建议他，我的意思是，他基本上连自己输了都不想承认。

sentences.en: Now, the most likely challenger is a man called Sir Keith Joseph, who had been Heath's Secretary of State for Health and Social Security.
sentences.zh: 现在，最可能的挑战者是一个叫基思·约瑟夫爵士的人，他曾担任希思的卫生和社会保障大臣。

sentences.en: He was an heir to a construction firm, Fortune.
sentences.zh: 他是建筑公司Fortune的继承人。

sentences.en: Doesn't he come out in favour of eugenics or something?
sentences.zh: 他不是支持优生学什么的吗？

sentences.en: Well, we're going to come to this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们马上就会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: We're going to come to this.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: He's a kind of Tory Robespierre, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他就像是托利党的罗伯斯庇尔，汤姆。

sentences.en: So he's pale.
sentences.zh: 他脸色苍白。

sentences.en: He's very priggish.
sentences.zh: 他非常拘谨。

sentences.en: He's incredibly serious.
sentences.zh: 他极其严肃。

sentences.en: He's incredibly conscientious.
sentences.zh: 他极其认真负责。

sentences.en: He's one of the rare Tauras, I think it's fair to say, who probably spends about 20 hours a day thinking about the plight of the poor.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，他是罕见的托利党人之一，可能每天花20个小时思考穷人的困境。

sentences.en: And he will physically writhe with agony.
sentences.zh: 他会因为痛苦而身体扭曲。

sentences.en: Isn't he a mad monk?
sentences.zh: 他不是个疯和尚吗？

sentences.en: People call him the mad monk.
sentences.zh: 人们叫他疯和尚。

sentences.en: They call him the mad monk.
sentences.zh: 他们叫他疯和尚。

sentences.en: And he undergoes this extraordinary conversion experience in the course of 1974.
sentences.zh: 他在1974年期间经历了一次非凡的转变。

sentences.en: So where all this is going on, from the kind of corporatist Toryism of the Heath era to free market radicalism.
sentences.zh: 从希思时代的社团主义托利主义转向了自由市场激进主义。

sentences.en: He says, I believed all this time I was a conservative.
sentences.zh: 他说：我一直以为自己是个保守派。

sentences.en: I see now I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 现在我明白了，我不是。

sentences.en: But just to be clear, I mean, we today associate conservatism with free market economics.
sentences.zh: 但要明确一点，我的意思是，我们今天将保守主义与自由市场经济联系在一起。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Principally because of Mrs. Thatcher and I guess Reagan as well.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为撒切尔夫人，我想还有里根。

sentences.en: But actually, letting the free market rip through institutions and people's livelihood and destroy industries and ways of living that have lasted for decades and often centuries.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，让自由市场冲击机构和人们的生计，摧毁持续了几十年甚至几个世纪的工业和生活方式。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not conservative really, is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那真的不是保守主义，对吧？

sentences.en: Ted Heath there on the podcaSt. Lovely to welcome him.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思在播客里。很高兴欢迎他。

sentences.en: But all the choices facing people in this period, whether on the far left, the right, whatever, are all awful.
sentences.zh: 但这一时期人们面临的所有选择，无论是极左、右翼还是其他什么，都很糟糕。

sentences.en: Pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Awful.
sentences.zh: 糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Theo has written in the chat, hence the term neoconservative.
sentences.zh: 西奥在聊天室里写道，所以才有了“新保守主义”这个词。

sentences.en: But actually, Theo, the real term is neoliberal.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，西奥，真正的术语是“新自由主义”。

sentences.en: So a lot of real Tom Holland style, well, the people that Tom was ventriloquizing, so sort of patrician consensual Tories who fought in tank battles in 1944.
sentences.zh: 所以很多真正的汤姆·霍兰风格的人，嗯，就是汤姆模仿的那种人，也就是1944年参加过坦克战的贵族共识派托利党人。

sentences.en: Thick glasses.
sentences.zh: 戴着厚眼镜。

sentences.en: Now with thick glasses.
sentences.zh: 现在戴着厚眼镜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They would say, this isn't really conservatism if it's free markets.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，如果这是自由市场，那这根本不是保守主义。

sentences.en: This is liberalism.
sentences.zh: 这是自由主义。

sentences.en: This is Victorian liberalism, and we don't want any part of it in our party.
sentences.zh: 这是维多利亚时代的自由主义，我们党内不需要这种东西。

sentences.en: And they would later say this of Mrs. Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 他们后来也会这样评价撒切尔夫人。

sentences.en: Now, Keith Joseph doesn't think this.
sentences.zh: 现在，基思·约瑟夫不这么认为。

sentences.en: He's been converted to this kind of neoliberalism.
sentences.zh: 他已经转变为这种新自由主义了。

sentences.en: And he says, we've done it all wrong.
sentences.zh: 他说：我们全做错了。

sentences.en: Everything that Ted Heath stood for is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 泰德·希思所代表的一切都是胡说八道。

sentences.en: All his friends are saying, come on, challenge Heath.
sentences.zh: 他所有的朋友都在说：来吧，挑战希思。

sentences.en: Put us on a free market line.
sentences.zh: 让我们走自由市场路线。

sentences.en: The tough medicine that is needed.
sentences.zh: 这是所需要的猛药。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: He's going to do it.
sentences.zh: 他要这么做了。

sentences.en: And Mrs. Thatcher will be his campaign manager.
sentences.zh: 而撒切尔夫人将成为他的竞选经理。

sentences.en: And then, like Enoch Powell before him, Joseph makes the terrible mistake of going to Birmingham to give a speech.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像之前的伊诺克·鲍威尔一样，约瑟夫犯了一个可怕的错误，去伯明翰发表演讲。

sentences.en: And he goes to the Grand Hotel in Birmingham, and he gives this disastrous speech where he says, and I quote, the balance of our population, our human stock is threatened.
sentences.zh: 他去了伯明翰的大酒店，发表了那场灾难性的演讲，他说，引用一下，“我们人口的平衡，我们的人类种群受到了威胁”。

sentences.en: And he says it's threatened because a high and rising proportion of children are being born to mothers least fitted to bring children into the world.
sentences.zh: 他说受到威胁是因为，出生在最不适合抚养孩子的母亲身上的孩子比例很高，而且还在不断上升。

sentences.en: And he says we should make a massive effort to get working class women to use more birth control, to stop them having children.
sentences.zh: 他说我们应该做出巨大努力，让工人阶级女性更多地使用避孕措施，以阻止她们生育。

sentences.en: And he says, because if we don't, it'll mean the degeneration of Britain.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为如果我们不这样做，就意味着英国的退化。

sentences.en: The degeneration of the racial stock.
sentences.zh: 种族血统的退化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Is he kind of verging on saying that?
sentences.zh: 他这是在暗示这一点吗？

sentences.en: Well, he doesn't use the words racial stock.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他并没有使用“种族血统”这个词。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这样说很公道，汤姆。

sentences.en: And I think he would be appalled.
sentences.zh: 而且我想他会感到震惊的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's Jewish himself, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他自己就是犹太人。

sentences.en: Harold Macmillan, rather cruelly, said he was the only boring Jew I've ever known.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·麦克米伦曾相当刻薄地说，他是他所认识的唯一一个无聊的犹太人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I think a lot of people are absolutely appalled by this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想很多人对此感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: They think it's the most terrible gaffe.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一个极其严重的失言。

sentences.en: Private Eye, which we mentioned a few times in the satirical magazine, because of his enthusiasm for birth control, took to calling him Sashith instead of Sakeith.
sentences.zh: 我们在讽刺杂志《私家侦探》中提到过几次，因为他热衷于节育，杂志社开始叫他“萨西斯”而不是“萨基斯”。

sentences.en: And I think people just thought he's gone mad, you know, and he basically thinks, oh, I've made a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 我想人们只是觉得他疯了，你知道，他自己也觉得，哦，我犯了一个可怕的错误。

sentences.en: And he effectively bows out.
sentences.zh: 于是他实际上退出了。

sentences.en: He goes around the House of Commons in November.
sentences.zh: 十一月的时候，他在下议院四处走动。

sentences.en: So, it's only six weeks or so after the election, saying to people, oh, I can't, I'm not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 那时距离选举才过去六周左右，他跟人说，哦，我不行，我不打算干了。

sentences.en: Because, also, he's not really cut out to be a leader anyway.
sentences.zh: 因为，说到底，他本来就不是当领导的料。

sentences.en: He's a kind of Prince Hamlet figure, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他就像个哈姆雷特王子式的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is an absolute, he's dithery.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是，他优柔寡断。

sentences.en: He delays.
sentences.zh: 他总是拖延。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's intellectual.
sentences.zh: 他是个知识分子。

sentences.en: People would often say of him, he's the only person they would meet, who in meetings would genuinely strike his own head very hard.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，他是他们见过的唯一一个在开会时会真用力敲自己脑袋的人。

sentences.en: When he was changing his mind, he'd, like, pummel his head and stuff, which they found disconcerting.
sentences.zh: 当他改变主意时，他会捶打自己的头之类的，这让人们感到不安。

sentences.en: So, anyway, on the 21st of November, he goes into the office of his campaign manager and he says, Margaret, I'm not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 总之，11月21日，他走进竞选经理的办公室说：“玛格丽特，我不打算干了。”

sentences.en: And it's at that point, there's no doubt that it hadn't occurred to her before then, because she wanted to be Chancellor, not Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，毫无疑问，在此之前她从未想过这一点，因为她想当的是财政大臣，而不是首相。

sentences.en: It's at that point that she said to him, well, Keith, if you're not going to stand, I will.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，她对他说：“好吧，基思，如果你不打算参选，那我就选。”

sentences.en: And then she goes home and she says to Dennis, her husband, I'm actually going to stand myself for the Tory leadership against Ted Heath.
sentences.zh: 然后她回家对丈夫丹尼斯说，我真的要亲自参加保守党领袖竞选，对抗泰德·希思。

sentences.en: And Dennis said, you must be out of your mind.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯说，你一定是疯了。

sentences.en: You haven't got hope.
sentences.zh: 你一点希望都没有。

sentences.en: You haven't got hope.
sentences.zh: 你一点希望都没有。

sentences.en: And so, four days later, she ignores Dennis, obviously.
sentences.zh: 于是，四天后，她显然没理会丹尼斯。

sentences.en: Four days later, she goes to see Ted Heath in his office and she says to him, Ted, I'm going to stand against you for the leadership or whatever.
sentences.zh: 四天后，她去办公室见了泰德·希思，对他说：“泰德，我要参加领袖竞选，和你竞争。”

sentences.en: And Ted Heath, all he says is, you'll lose.
sentences.zh: 而泰德·希思只说了句：“你会输的。”

sentences.en: And Tom, the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: So, so much more to come.
sentences.zh: 还有更多精彩内容。

sentences.zh: 70年代，工党政府。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: We should get on to that next year, because next year will be the anniversary, Tom, of her becoming Tory leader.
sentences.zh: 我们明年应该继续讲这个，因为明年就是她成为保守党领袖的周年纪念了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.zh: 所以，这是制作一系列关于70年代末节目的绝佳机会。

sentences.zh: 那么，詹姆斯·卡拉汉。

sentences.en: I mean, the public, I think, I mean, they're desperate to hear a series of podcasts about James Callaghan.
sentences.zh: 我是说，公众，我想，他们非常渴望听到一系列关于詹姆斯·卡拉汉的播客。

sentences.en: People have been repeatedly demanding it, and so it will come.
sentences.zh: 人们一直在反复要求，所以它会来的。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We hope that you have all enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 我们希望大家都喜欢这一期。

sentences.zh: 我得说，这让我振作了不少。

sentences.zh: 我对国家的现状感到沮丧。

sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.zh: 我心想，好吧，情况还没到最坏的地步。

sentences.zh: 哦，汤姆，能以让你感到更愉快的方式结束播客真是太好了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
